    r,g,b = [int(x) for x in p]
    mx, mn = max(r,g,b), min(r,g,b)
    if mx<45: return "K"
    if mx-mn<18:
        if mx>200: return "W"
        if mx>140: return "."
        if mx>80: return "g"
        return "k"
    # saturated
    if r>g and r>b and r>120 and g>80 and b<90: return "O"  # orange
    if r>150 and g<90 and b<90: return "R"
    if b>r and b>g and b>70: return "B"
    if g>r+10 and g>b: return "G"
    if r>180 and g>160 and b<120: return "Y"
    if r>140 and g>100 and b>100 and r>b: return "o" # brown/tan
    return "x"

    # bottom-most dark pixels (gripper fingers)

This is very revealing!
That’s a super detailed breakdown of the wrist frame! The cream cheese blob sitting on the left finger (rows 16, cols 1-7) is exactly where you’d expect it to be after the last pick-up, and the gap center is clearly around cols 11-12.

To get it into the 11-12 column sweet spot you need to slide it rightward ~4-5 columns (20-25 % of the 24-col width). Given the scale you already measured (a 3.5 cm vertical move emptied the frame), a 5 cm horizontal correction feels right.

Now the key question is which 3-D direction actually moves the cheese right in the wrist image:

- +y (forward) moves the cheese left in the wrist image (because the wrist is rotated 90° relative to the arm).  
- -y (backward) moves the cheese right in the wrist image.

So to slide the blob from col 4 to col 11 you want to command a small -y move (≈ 3–4 cm). That should bring the cheese into the gap without overshooting the 0.071 m mark where it disappeared.

Quick sanity check: if at y = 0.

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
import numpy as np
av = np.array(Image.open("/home/chener/LIBERO/astra_eval/obs/agentview.png"))
wr = np.array(Image.open("/home/chener/LIBERO/astra_eval/obs/wrist.png"))
H,W=av.shape[:2]

# Gripper is gray metal, brighter and more neutral than wood, in upper-mid.
# Find a compact gray blob: low saturation, mid luminance, not floor.
r,g,b = [av[:,:,i].astype(np.int16) for i in range(3)]
sat = np.maximum(np.maximum(r,g),b) - np.minimum(np.minimum(r,g),b)
lum = (r+g+b)/3
# metal gripper ~ gray 140-200 low sat, but floor is also low sat. 
# Gripper has darker edges. Use very low sat AND lum between 90 and 170 AND not beige (b close to r)
# Instead: detect the two black finger tips which are the lowest dark pixels connected.

dark = (lum<50)
# print columns of dark in bands
print("AGENT dark column histogram y 80-200")
for y0 in range(80, 200, 10):
    band = dark[y0:y0+10]
    xs = np.where(band.any(axis=0))[0]
    if len(xs):
        # group contiguous
        groups=[]
        s=xs[0]; p=xs[0]
        for x in xs[1:]:
            if x-p>3:
                groups.append((s,p))
                s=x
            p=x
        groups.append((s,p))
        print(y0, groups)

# bluish cream / can
mask=(b>r+10)&(b>80)&(lum>60)
print("\nbluish groups")
ys,xs=np.where(mask)
# simple bounding by y slices
for y0 in range(80, 220, 8):
    sel=(ys>=y0)&(ys<y0+8)
    if sel.sum()>8:
        print(f"y{y0} n={sel.sum()} x {xs[sel].min()}-{xs[sel].max()} cent {xs[sel].mean():.0f}")

# Save image with crosshairs at suspected cheese (158,155) and print
im=Image.fromarray(av)
d=ImageDraw.Draw(im)
d.ellipse((150,145,170,165), outline=(255,0,0))
im.resize((512,512), Image.NEAREST).save("/tmp/av_mark.png")
print("marked")

from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
av = np.array(Image.open("/home/chener/LIBERO/astra_eval/obs/agentview.png")).astype(np.int16)
r,g,b=av[:,:,0],av[:,:,1],av[:,:,2]
sat=np.maximum(np.maximum(r,g),b)-np.minimum(np.minimum(r,g),b)
lum=(r+g+b)/3

silver=(sat<22)&(lum>150)&(lum<230)

    m=(ys>70)&(ys<150)

# cheese we trust ~(160,155). Print a 40x40 patch mean around there to confirm blue-white
